additional_info.subject: RE: ID0479455-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP / R9 170002566] Logs Check CRM:00263000463
additional_info.body:
Dear Rosita,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0479455.
The ticket has been opened for issues to charge on 19.02.2025 on charger
MP/R9 170002566.
I analyzed the logs, and here are my findings:
#2 charging session has been attempted, both on DC2, one at 2026-02-19T13:24:53 and one at 2026-02-19T13:54:00
Both sessions failed because the Backend did not send information to the charger in regards of authentication.
As a matter of fact, the charger was experiencing a sever toggling of the OCPP connection in that period, with the connection to the Backend going very often online and then offline. This happened also during the authentication phase, and the charger did not receive the messages from the Backend.
I checked the logs, and I could find also the values related to signal strength and internet connection of the router:
The values show a good/fair to good internet connection:
The RSRP represents the power of LTE signal, as its values are considered as good
The SINR represents the rate of information transferred, and its values are very good
The RSRQ represents the quality rate of information transferred, and it is fairly good
Overall, the connectivity of the router XF4 was good, but the Backend kept closing the communication with the router (hence the charger).
In conclusion, the sessions failed because the charger was not able to receive the authentication info from the Backend, as the Backend kept closing the communication channel with the charger. Please let me know if I can close this ticket, as no issue has been detected from charger side.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0479455-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP / R9 170002566] Logs Check CRM:00263000463
additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Rosita,
we have received the case from our colleague Fosco Servidei, a technical expert at Headquarters. After analyzing the logs related to the ticket’s opening date, we identified a backend connection error characterized by a loop of the OCPP connection going online and offline.
As mentioned by our colleague, the charger, following standard configuration, requests a response from the backend regarding the connection status every 30 seconds. As shown in the attached log, the responses alternate between "OCPP connection closed" and "OCPP connection established."
We would like to proceed with a joint analysis with the NTT Data team to understand what is observed on the backend side and to evaluate the possible cause of this behavior together.
We will share updates as soon as possible.
Best regards,
CANCELLIERI, Giuseppe (SI E EU IT)
